first_registration: Real HandleRegisterNode writes serialized ALIVE data; original manager is destroyed after its callbacks complete.
restore: New manager caches are asserted empty; existing LoadInitData calls GcsInitData::AsyncLoad; production Initialize restores the head.
replay: Same serialized RegisterNodeRequest; same node lifetime and ID; no cache mutations by test.
publication_observer: Production GcsPublisher using existing FakePublisher, recording both node channels.
storage_backend: Existing InMemoryStoreClient retained across manager lifetimes; GcsTableStorage wrapper retained.
limitations: No physical GCS process crash or disk/Redis recovery in new unit test.
No transport-level lost reply or automatic gRPC retry injection.
No real raylet, health checker, subscriber delivery or NodeRemoved fatal execution in new unit test.
No concurrent independent death/write-completion race injection.
No exactly-once notification guarantee: one ALIVE publication per channel was observed on replay in both variants.
TestGcsTableReload/1 returns early for memory; its PASS is not a recovery exercise.
Redis TestGcsTableReload/0 and registration tests execute real GCS client/server paths, but do not combine a lost reply with recovery replay.
phase1_race: Remains a hypothesis; not tested or attributed to this PR.
